headline: Students lock CUET VC inside office for 12 hours
summary: Protesters demand the resignation of the new Vice Chancellor after he entered the administrative building by breaking a lock.
details: Students at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) have locked the new Vice Chancellor, Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, inside his office building for 12 hours.
The incident occurred on Monday after the VC entered his office by breaking the lock of the administrative building's main gate, accompanied by Chhatra League activists.
Protesters locked the main gate at 12:30 PM after the VC failed to leave the building by a deadline they had set.
The VC, along with several others including the president of the CUET Chhatra League, remained trapped inside. Students also disconnected the electricity supply to the building.
The unrest stems from demands to reinstate former VC Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem, who was removed from the office.
Teachers, officials, and employees have joined the students in a 'total shutdown' and 'total non-cooperation' program, halting all academic activities for nearly three weeks.
An Assistant Commissioner (Land) from Raozan visited the campus to negotiate, requesting that electricity and water be provided to those trapped inside.
Students stated they will only restore electricity and other facilities once the Vice Chancellor resigns.
caption:
A university VC is trapped in his own office for 12 hours after students locked the main gate and cut the power.

Students at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) have locked the new Vice Chancellor, Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, inside his office building for 12 hours.

The incident occurred on Monday after the VC entered his office by breaking the lock of the administrative building's main gate, accompanied by Chhatra League activists.

Protesters locked the main gate at 12:30 PM after the VC failed to leave the building by a deadline they had set.

The VC, along with several others including the president of the CUET Chhatra League, remained trapped inside. Students also disconnected the electricity supply to the building.

The unrest stems from demands to reinstate former VC Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem, who was removed from the office.

Teachers, officials, and employees have joined the students in a 'total shutdown' and 'total non-cooperation' program, halting all academic activities for nearly three weeks.

An Assistant Commissioner (Land) from Raozan visited the campus to negotiate, requesting that electricity and water be provided to those trapped inside.

Students stated they will only restore electricity and other facilities once the Vice Chancellor resigns.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: 5,418 passengers stranded as [[51 flights from Dhaka grounded]] due to Saudi crisis
headline: 5,418 passengers stranded as 51 flights from Dhaka grounded due to Saudi crisis
summary: Flight disruptions from Saturday night to Monday afternoon have left thousands of travelers affected, including those on direct and transit flights to Saudi Arabia.
details: Restrictions on flight operations at Saudi Arabian airports have led to the disruption of 51 flights from Dhaka, affecting 5,418 passengers.
According to a press release from the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) on Monday, the disruptions occurred between Saturday night and Monday afternoon.
Of the total 51 disrupted flights, 12 were direct flights to Saudi Arabia, including services by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Saudia, and Riyadh Air.
The remaining 39 were transit flights operated by airlines such as IndiGo, SalamAir, Emirates, Qatar Airways, and flydubai.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Saudi Arabia has urged expatriates to remain alert and cautious amid the ongoing situation.
Many passengers, including migrant workers, have reported significant distress and uncertainty regarding their travel plans and livelihoods.
caption:
Over 5,000 passengers stranded. 51 flights from Dhaka grounded due to Saudi Arabian airport restrictions.

Restrictions on flight operations at Saudi Arabian airports have led to the disruption of 51 flights from Dhaka, affecting 5,418 passengers.

According to a press release from the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) on Monday, the disruptions occurred between Saturday night and Monday afternoon.

Of the total 51 disrupted flights, 12 were direct flights to Saudi Arabia, including services by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Saudia, and Riyadh Air.

The remaining 39 were transit flights operated by airlines such as IndiGo, SalamAir, Emirates, Qatar Airways, and flydubai.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Saudi Arabia has urged expatriates to remain alert and cautious amid the ongoing situation.

Many passengers, including migrant workers, have reported significant distress and uncertainty regarding their travel plans and livelihoods.
